messages.subject: SEM Fundamentals: Basic question on covariances
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to model attrition using SEM. Following is the model I am using:

models$k3 <- 
    ' Loyalty =~ JobLevel + TotalWorkingYears + YearsAtCompany + YearsInCurrentRole + YearsSinceLastPromotion + YearsWithCurrManager+Age+NumCompaniesWorked
Seniority =~ JobLevel + z1 + TotalWorkingYears +Age+NumCompaniesWorked
z2~Seniority+Loyalty+DistanceFromHome+EnvironmentSatisfaction+JobInvolvement+JobSatisfaction
YearsInCurrentRole ~~    YearsWithCurrManager
'


When I run the last line of code, I was reccomended to add the following relations ( which will significantly improve the model):
Seniority  ~  z2
JobLevel ~~ z1
TotalWorkingYears ~~ Age

However, I have the following questions:
  1. I have already regressed z2 on Seniority. Why is lavaan specifying me to define an inverse regression relationship between the variables as well? What does this mean conceptually?How will it improve my model?
  2. As per other reccomendations, I can improve my model by specifying a covariance relation between JobLevel and Age. However, I have already specified a common factor Loyalty to capture the communality between these two variables. Similary, Seniority captures the covariance between TotalWorkingYears and Age. Is it because there is extra covariance between the reccomended pairs which are not reflected in other manifest variables (used to determine the same factor)?What is the difference between letting the variables correlate explicitly and specifying them as manifest variables for the same factor in the same model?
  3. What will be the difference,conceptually, between estimating a regression parameter and a covariance parameter between the same variables?For instance, specifying:
               JobLevel ~~ z1 vs JobLevel ~ z1

I am probably asking extremely naive questions here. But I would really appreciate if someone can take time to answer them.

parts: I have also posted my questions on SEMNET.However, I would like to know the logic that went behind coding the function 'modificationindices'  i.e how does it check for improvements in the model chi-square value. Is it simply a hit-and-trial technique wherein various models are run incrementally (adding one hypothesis at a time) and chi-square improvements are chalked out?

That's still a SEMNET question because modification indices are available in all SEM packages, not a lavaan-specific feature.  Here is a seminal article talking about the use and misuse of modification indices. 

http://www.jstor.org/stable/271030

A quick Google search should turn up a host of other literature on the topic, which is still an active area of research.
